techStack: React 18 with TypeScript; functional components using useCallback, useState, useContext, useEffect, useLayoutEffect
Functional state updaters (prev => ...) are the required pattern for concurrent-safe Set mutations
fetch API for server persistence; no third-party HTTP library
Vitest + React Testing Library; pnpm test / pnpm build for verification
No additional libraries needed — all required APIs (useState, useCallback, finally) are already in use
features: toggleFavourite: optimistic update of favouriteIds already works; two bugs: (1) setPendingIds never called so isPending always false, (2) catch block never reverts the optimistic update
isFavourite: correctly reads from favouriteIds — no change needed
isPending: correctly reads from pendingIds — no change needed; pendingIds is declared and wired into context but never populated
FavouriteButton: already reads isPending and applies disabled + sr-only 'Loading' span — must not be modified
localStorage persistence via useEffect on favouriteIds — must remain intact
setError in catch block — must remain; fix only adds alongside it, does not replace it
architecture: Single context provider (FavouritesProvider) owns all state; FavouritesContext.tsx is the only file to change
toggleFavourite is a useCallback closure; wasAdded is correctly captured before the optimistic update — already safe
Fix location: inside toggleFavourite, before the try block (add to pendingIds), inside the catch block (revert favouriteIds), and in a new finally block (remove from pendingIds)
Functional updater form setFavouriteIds(prev => ...) required in catch to operate on latest state, not a stale snapshot
Functional updater form setPendingIds(prev => ...) required for both add and remove to avoid concurrent-toggle races
edgeCases: Concurrent toggles on different products: catch block MUST use functional updater setFavouriteIds(prev => ...) rather than restoring a full-Set snapshot — a snapshot revert would overwrite concurrently-settled changes to other products (Req 8)

finally cleanup must not be duplicated in try and catch separately — a single finally block satisfies both Req 6 (pending cleared on success) and Req 7 (pending cleared on failure) without code duplication
Rapid double-click is blocked at UI level by disabled state once pending tracking is added; no extra guard needed in toggleFavourite itself
setError call in catch must be preserved so the error remains surfaced to the UI — the fix adds setFavouriteIds revert alongside it
wasAdded must be read before the optimistic setFavouriteIds call (already the case); the catch block uses wasAdded to determine which direction to revert

tasks.requirement: Req 5, 6, 7 — isPending(id) must return true while fetch is in-flight and false after it settles (success or failure); FavouriteButton must be disabled with 'Loading' text during the request
tasks.description: In toggleFavourite, add setPendingIds(prev => { const next = new Set(prev); next.add(productId); return next; }) immediately before the try block. Add a finally block after the catch block that calls setPendingIds(prev => { const next = new Set(prev); next.delete(productId); return next; }) to clear pending state regardless of outcome.

tasks.requirement: Req 3, 4, 8 — optimistic update must be reverted when the fetch rejects; revert must use a functional updater to avoid overwriting concurrent-settled state for other products
tasks.description: In the catch block of toggleFavourite, after the existing setError(...) call, add setFavouriteIds(prev => { const next = new Set(prev); if (wasAdded) { next.delete(productId); } else { next.add(productId); } return next; }) to undo the optimistic update using the captured wasAdded flag and a functional updater operating on latest state.
